body.cap: ​A participant and buyer talking with each other in the Gyeonggi Province Pavilion at CES 2023 │Photo Courtesy - Gyeonggido Business & Science Accelerator​

body.x: Eight SMEs based in Gyeonggi province engaged in 162 export negotiation talks worth $9.52 million at CES 2023, the world's largest electronics and IT exhibition.

The Gyeonggi Provincial Government and Gyeonggido Business & Science Accelerator said they organized the Gyeonggi Province Pavilion and made such a great achievement at Consumer Electronics Show (CES) 2023 held in Las Vegas, U.S., from Thursday, January 5 to Sunday, January 8 in local time.

With about 2,400 businesses from around the world participating in the exhibition, future technologies such as smart home, food tech, Web3 and the metaverse, robotics, and future mobility for energy saving and security enhancement to improve efficiency were presented.
At CES 2023, a total of 486 Korean businesses participated. They ranked second only to the United States in terms of the number of participants, promoting Korea's status as an “IT powerhouse.”

In the Gyeonggi Province Pavilion, eight SMEs with outstanding quality competitiveness exhibited various products. In particular, a Bucheon-based inactive battery manufacturer Cosmos Lab Co., Ltd., a mobile energy storage device manufacturer aeonus Co., Ltd., and a maker of multi-functional food for probiotics vegans Gwangjin Co., Ltd., drew a lot of attention from visitors.

The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Hee-ryong Won, visited the Gyeonggi Province Pavilion with an advisory group and showed a great interest in products from Cosmos Lab, which makes non-ignitable batteries available for direct application to electric vehicles, praising the business for producing what can replace Chinese products in Korea.

According to Cosmos Lab’s CEO Ju-Hyuk Lee, “By attending this exhibition, we were able to accurately understand global technology as well as consumption trends and demands while expanding our business with an R&D partnership offer from Boeing, an airplane manufacture.”

Participating companies spoke highly of the Gyeonggi Provincial Government and Gyeonggido Business & Science Accelerator (GBSA) for setting up and running booths in CES Eureka Park which can be inaccessible as an individual business and for supporting them with interpretation, consultation, and shipping expenses. They appreciated all of the support, which substantially helped to bring about the favorable results. Eureka Park only allows startups with innovative products and technology certified by CTA (Consumer Technology Association) to participate.

Meanwhile, CES is regarded as one of the world's three largest IT exhibitions and the largest of the three by participants. The Gyeonggi Provincial Government expects that attending the exhibition will lay a foundation for its businesses to utilize the positive perception of Korean products as being advanced in the IT field and to enter the global market. It also plans to maximize the outcomes by actively supporting the participants with export-related follow-up covering contracts, paperwork, and expert consulting services.
